```python
read_torch_bin(path) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
```

Part of [`evoxc_hf.weights`](/api/evoxc-hf/weights/)

Read a `pytorch_model.bin` checkpoint (zip **or** legacy format).

The format is decided by content (`zipfile.is_zipfile`), not by name.
Tensors are rebuilt from their storages through a restricted unpickler
(`_RestrictedUnpickler`), so tensor views, offsets, strides and
transposed views are all honoured while arbitrary pickled code is
rejected. A `{"state_dict": {...}}` wrapper is unwrapped; a non-dict
unpickled object or a non-tensor state-dict entry raises
`~evoxc_hf.errors.HFWeightError`. Dtypes follow the module dtype
policy (f16/bf16 → f32). No key mapping and no transposition happens here —
that is the per-family canonicaliser's job.

Storage blobs are laid out differently in the two formats: the zip format
stores each storage as a bare `*/data/<key>` member (no length prefix),
while the legacy format appends, per listed key, an 8-byte little-endian
int64 element count followed by that storage's raw bytes — the count is
validated against the pickle stream and the file must be consumed exactly.

[View Python source](https://github.com/EMI-Group/evoxc/blob/main/evoxc_hf/src/evoxc_hf/weights.py#L586)
